clue.text: Monarch rejected hatred — that's a relief

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the monarch's abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina, a monarch
spite is malicious hatred

explanation.surface: A subject sighs with relief after the king spurns a hateful courtier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monarch' points to the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth, and 'relief' means a break, not comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or reprieve from something unpleasant.

clue.text: Quality of pictures in hotel foyer

definitions.meaning: how well a television or radio picks up a signal
the front desk area where guests check in

explanation.surface: A hotel lobby has a television with a fine picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Reception is both how well a broadcast signal is received and the check-in area of a hotel.

clue.text: Start to slip and fall?

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: a tumble is a fall

explanation.surface: Someone begins to lose their footing and wonders if they will go down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' takes S from slip; the whole clue also describes the answer, a slip that begins a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to trip and lurch, as if about to go over.

clue.text: Rational judgment seen in, say, shock treatment

parts.note: taken as written
to tell is to say
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, an electric shock treatment

explanation.surface: Clear thinking is evident in electric shock therapy, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a piece of the answer, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellect is the faculty of reasoning and understanding.

clue.text: Send off part of remittance required

indicators.note: part of means the letters are a stretch inside the next word

explanation.surface: Someone has to post part of a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give out or discharge, sending something out.

clue.text: Form of protection favoured by soldier

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
a pet pupil is a favoured one

explanation.surface: A trooper prefers a particular kind of defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or rampart.

clue.text: Amicably changing sides just before the end would be a joke

indicators.text: changing sides just before the end
indicators.note: sides are right and left, so the right near the finish becomes a left

parts.note: a pleasantry is a light joke

explanation.surface: A friendly debater who switches sides at the last moment would be a laughing stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides just before the end' swaps R (right) for L (left) in the penultimate letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantly means in an agreeable, friendly manner.

clue.text: The bloodier the better

definitions.meaning: of steak, more undercooked and red inside
more exceptional or choice, as with a finer thing

explanation.surface: A gore-loving motto: the bloodier the better.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare steak is lightly cooked and red, and something rare is uncommon and so prized.

clue.text: To identify unpleasant smell is not a cure

parts.note: to place someone is to identify or recognise them
BO is body odour, an unpleasant smell

explanation.surface: Being able to name a nasty odour does not fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy medicine with no active ingredient, given for its psychological effect.

clue.text: Negotiate for free entertainment

definitions.meaning: something paid for by another, as when a host stands you a meal

explanation.surface: Bargaining over complimentary entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with someone is to negotiate, and a treat is an outing someone else pays for.

clue.text: French vineyard and French wine bottle

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine, as in grand cru
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A French vineyard produces both wine and the bottle it comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruet is a small glass bottle for oil or vinegar, and also for communion wine.

clue.text: One beer ain't enough, perhaps, for him

definitions.text: One beer ain't enough, perhaps, for him

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be in some other order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A drinker for whom one pint never suffices.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus BEER and AINT is rearranged; the whole clue also describes the drunkard, whose motto is that one beer is never enough.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard, someone who keeps drinking past the first glass.

clue.text: Piece of rock — dashed for cover

definitions.text: Piece of rock — dashed for cover

parts.words: Piece of rock — dashed for cover
parts.note: a small stone, which when dashed against wet render makes a common British wall covering

explanation.surface: A chunk of stone is hurled at something to protect it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pebbledash is a British exterior wall finish of small stones thrown onto wet plaster, so the stone dashed gives the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a small smooth stone, a little piece of rock.

clue.text: Greedy with hunger, I use rent improperly

indicators.note: improperly means the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A starving tenant confesses to misusing the money meant for rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for hungry or greedy, from the Latin for to be hungry.

clue.text: Former partner gets the bird inside and outside

indicators.note: inside means the bird is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former
an ally is a partner
a tern is a sea bird

explanation.surface: An ex has a bird indoors and outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Externally means on the outer side or from without.

clue.text: One French man and woman

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
René is a common French man's name

explanation.surface: A list of people: a single Frenchman and a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's given name, from the Greek for peace.

clue.text: Scared of outsiders, one withdraws from other races

definitions.text: Scared of outsiders, one withdraws from other races

parts.words: Scared of outsiders, one withdraws from other races
parts.note: a description of a person who fears strangers and foreigners and keeps away from other peoples

explanation.surface: A timid person shrinks from foreigners and keeps aloof from other peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'races' looks like competitions to drop out of, but it means peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A xenophobe fears or hates strangers and foreigners, from the Greek for stranger plus fear.

clue.text: Fundamental truth star proclaimed

indicators.note: proclaimed means spoken out, so the word is taken for how it is pronounced

parts.note: the principal is the leading performer, the star of a show

explanation.surface: A celebrity announces a basic truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proclaimed' turns the star, PRINCIPAL, into its same-sounding twin.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle is a basic truth or law that underlies a system of thought.

clue.text: Another line put in granny flat, for example

definitions.meaning: an additional telephone line installed elsewhere in a building
a granny flat is a British term for a self-contained annex for an elderly relative, a building added on

explanation.surface: A second phone line is installed in the annex.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is both an extra telephone on the same line and an addition built onto a house.

clue.text: One may be pushed to admit a late entry

definitions.text: One may be pushed to admit a late entry

parts.words: One may be pushed to admit a late entry
parts.note: something pressed by a caller arriving after dark, so the door is opened for them; admit reads like confess

explanation.surface: A latecomer is pressured into confessing a tardy submission.
explanation.definitionFit: A night bell is a doorbell for use after hours, rung by someone needing a doctor or porter at night.

clue.text: Look around 'orrible place for antelope

indicators.note: around means the look is placed around the place

parts.note: to gaze is to look
the dropped h of 'orrible signals a dropped h in hell, the horrible place

explanation.surface: A Cockney looks around a dreadful spot in search of an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orrible is horrible with its H dropped, telling you to drop the H of HELL too.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazelle is a small graceful antelope of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Addition to book for teachers' training

definitions.meaning: an extra page or leaf set into a book
The British acronym for in-service training days for teachers

explanation.surface: Teachers on a training day get a supplement for their textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: INSET days are the British school days set aside for in-service teacher training while pupils stay home.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is an extra piece inserted into a book or a small map within a larger one.

clue.text: Put up with change he hates

indicators.note: change means the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a change he loathes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' is not tolerate but what one does with a sword after use.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a sword is to return it to its scabbard.

clue.text: Confusing viewers with brilliance

definitions.meaning: viewers are eyes, and bright light blinds and bewilders them

explanation.surface: Viewers are bewildered by a brilliant display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' looks like an audience, but it means eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dazzling light temporarily blinds the eyes, and dazzling things are strikingly brilliant.

clue.text: Name excellent sheikhdom

parts.note: to dub is to name
A1 is first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: Calling a sheikhdom first-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the emirates of the UAE, ruled by a sheikh.

clue.text: Gently wash the Spanish jacket part

parts.note: waves lap a shore, washing it gently
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spaniard washes part of a jacket gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a jacket below the collar.

clue.text: Containing loose stones with pole, wire netting

indicators.note: with means the pole's letter is placed alongside the stones

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose stones on a mountain slope
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A frame of wire mesh on a post holds back loose rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing' says the answer is made up of these pieces; 'pole' is a magnetic pole, not a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen can be a mesh of wire, as in a window screen or a sieve for gravel.

clue.text: One little sibling is a divine creature

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
sis is a short word for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: A younger sister is an angel.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is an Egyptian goddess, a deity.

clue.text: Yanks operate these to summon help

definitions.text: Yanks operate these to summon help

parts.words: Yanks operate these to summon help
parts.note: Yanks reads as Americans but means sharp tugs, the action that rings for servants

explanation.surface: Americans work certain devices to call for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Bell pulls are cords in grand houses tugged to ring for a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell pull is a cord or handle that rings a bell when pulled to call staff.

clue.text: Play on green with one's cherubic children

parts.note: to putt is to play a stroke on a golf green
I, the Roman numeral, is one; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: Angelic little children play putting together.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are figures of chubby naked infants in Renaissance art, like cupids.

clue.text: I do business extremely lucratively in optimal circumstances

parts.note: to deal is to trade or do business

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A trader boasts of making very good money when conditions are perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of lucratively, L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in the best possible situation, as things would be at their best.

clue.text: That woman was vulgar in low drinking dive

parts.note: she is the pronoun for that woman
'been' in place of 'was' or 'have been' is nonstandard, so a vulgar way of saying was

explanation.surface: A woman behaved coarsely in a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or Scottish drinking den, a disreputable illegal bar.
